idleGreeting.text: I'm here! I'll pipe up when something needs your attention, or tap me any time for a pointer.

tip1.text: Password and OTP live in your account settings, not here - I'm a snail-phone, not a locksmith.

tip2.text: Your session renews itself while you work. If it ever sinks, we chart you straight back to the login page.

tip1.text: An expired invitation isn't lost at sea - resend it and the clock resets to seven days.

tip2.text: Grant a role now? The crewmate sees it shortly, not instantly - even gull-mail takes its time.

tip3.text: The last ADMIN is protected - a ship with no captain just drifts in circles.

tip1.text: A permission with nobody holding it is dead weight - delete it, or grant it to a role from the matrix.

tip2.text: Groups collapse by default so the list stays readable - click one open to see what it guards.

tip3.text: At least one role must always hold roles:manage, or nobody's left who can fix the crew's roster.

tip1.text: The ship's log is never erased. Not even the sharpest first mate can rewrite a route already sailed.

tip2.text: Here you see who did what, and when - handy when someone swears they never touched a thing.

tip1.text: A language's code can't change once created - delete it and add a fresh one if you got the letters wrong.

tip2.text: Adding a language here makes it required on every in-progress draft's next submission - already-published content is untouched.

tip1.text: Tap a counter to open its status page: there you claim, approve or publish right from the row, without opening the card.

tip2.text: On the Draft and In review pages you can narrow the list to your own drafts, or to the reviews you hold - the rest of the crew's work stays one tap away.

tip1.text: Every entry sails the same route: draft, review, publishing. Nobody reviews what they wrote themselves.

tip2.text: The romaji is unique and shared by every language: change it and it changes for IT and EN alike.

tip3.text: Every version stays in the log: from an older one you can open a new draft and send it back through review.

refused.stale: Arrr! The version changed in the meantime: here it is as it stands now.
refused.failed: Arrr! That did not work. Try again in a moment.

reject.title: Reject this review?
reject.body: The content becomes Rejected and goes back to whoever wrote it, who will return it to draft to fix it. The reason is mandatory: it is what they will read to fix it.
reject.placeholder: What needs fixing before it goes back to review…
reject.hintShort: Required · at least one sentence ({{count}}/{{min}} characters)
reject.hintReady: Reason ready: the author will read it just like this.
reject.tooShort: The reason is mandatory: write what needs fixing, at least one sentence.

publish.title: Publish "{{name}}"?
publish.body: v{{version}} goes online, visible to every reader.
publish.bodyReplacing: v{{version}} goes online, visible to every reader. v{{online}} becomes "superseded" and stays in the history.
publish.note: Every version stays in the history, published or not.

archive.title: Archive "{{name}}"?
archive.body: v{{version}} stays approved but is not published: you will find it archived and can recover it whenever you like.
archive.note: Archiving is not retiring: this version has never been online.

retire.title: Retire v{{version}} from publication?
retire.body: Readers will no longer see it. Published versions stay in the history and can be republished.
retire.note: Retiring deletes nothing: the content moves to Retired.

restore.title: Republish v{{version}}?
restore.body: v{{version}} goes back online exactly as it was.
restore.bodyReplacing: v{{version}} goes back online exactly as it was. v{{online}}, online today, becomes "superseded" and stays in the history.
restore.note: No new version is created: an existing one is republished.

override.title: Act in {{owner}}'s place?

body.EDIT: You open {{owner}}'s draft v{{version}} for editing. It stays theirs: the author does not change.
body.SUBMIT: You submit {{owner}}'s v{{version}} for review in their place. {{owner}} stays the author.
body.PULL_BACK: You pull {{owner}}'s v{{version}} back from review: it goes back to draft.
body.RETURN_TO_DRAFT: You return {{owner}}'s rejected v{{version}} to draft in their place.
body.RELEASE: You take v{{version}} away from {{owner}}, who is reviewing it: it is free again for any reviewer.

override.note: The history will record that you did it, as an administrator.

legend.title: From here you can

DRAFT.EDIT: open the draft in the editor
DRAFT.SUBMIT: hand it to the reviewers; if fields are missing, the Den Den Mushi tells you which
DRAFT.DELETE: delete your draft, after a confirmation

IN_REVIEW.CLAIM: the review becomes yours, the others see it taken
IN_REVIEW.APPROVE: it moves to Ready to publish
IN_REVIEW.REJECT: back to its author with a mandatory reason
IN_REVIEW.RELEASE: puts it back in the queue for another reviewer
IN_REVIEW.PULL_BACK: brings one of yours back to draft

REJECTED.RETURN_TO_DRAFT: brings it back to draft to fix what the rejection says

READY_TO_PUBLISH.PUBLISH: puts it online for the readers
READY_TO_PUBLISH.ARCHIVE: sets it aside without publishing it

PUBLISHED.RETIRE: takes it off the site, it stays in the history
PUBLISHED.OPEN_NEW_VERSION: opens a new version; the online one stays until you publish

ARCHIVED.RECOVER: brings it back among the ready to publish
ARCHIVED.OPEN_NEW_VERSION: brings it back to work as a new version

RETIRED.OPEN_NEW_VERSION: opens a new version to review
